12.1: Arjuna's practical question: who is the better yogi — the one who worships you with form, or the one who seeks the imperishable unmanifest?
12.2: Those who fix their minds on Me and worship with supreme faith and steadfastness are, in My view, the most perfect.
12.3: But those who worship the imperishable, indefinable, unmanifest, all-pervading, unthinkable, immovable and eternal —
12.4: — restraining the senses, even-minded everywhere, delighting in the welfare of all beings, also reach Me.
12.5: The difficulty is greater for those set on the unmanifest; that goal is hard for the embodied to reach.
12.6: But those who surrender all actions to Me, hold Me supreme, and meditate on Me with undivided yoga —
12.7: — for them, whose minds are fixed on Me, I become the swift deliverer from the ocean of death and rebirth.
12.8: Fix your mind on Me alone, let your intellect dwell in Me, and you will live in Me hereafter — no doubt of this.
12.9: If you cannot fix the mind steadily on Me, seek to reach Me by the practice of repeated concentration.
12.10: If you are unable even to practise, be intent on doing work for My sake — you will attain perfection by that alone.
12.11: If even that is beyond you, take refuge in union with Me and renounce the fruit of all action with a controlled self.
12.12: Knowledge is better than practice, meditation better than knowledge, and renunciation of the fruit better still — peace follows renunciation.
12.13: The portrait of the devotee begins: hating none, friendly and compassionate, free of 'mine' and ego, even in pain and pleasure, forgiving.
12.14: Ever content, self-controlled, of firm resolve, with mind and intellect given to Me — that devotee is dear to Me.
12.15: One by whom the world is not agitated and who is not agitated by the world, free of joy, envy, fear and anxiety — dear to Me.
12.16: One who expects nothing, is pure, skilful, unconcerned, untroubled, renouncing every undertaking — that devotee is dear to Me.
12.17: One who neither rejoices nor hates nor grieves nor desires, renouncing good and evil, full of devotion — dear to Me.
12.18: Alike to foe and friend, in honour and dishonour, in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, free from attachment —
12.19: — indifferent to praise and blame, silent, content with anything, homeless, steady-minded and full of devotion — that one is dear to Me.
12.20: Those who follow this nectar of dharma as taught, with faith, holding Me supreme — those devotees are exceedingly dear to Me.
